1907.name: Array Max & Min
1907.note: class=prim primResID 1907 = Array Max & Min (NI docs functions/array-max-min.html, Programming>Array): returns max value, its first index, min value, its first index. Connector pane confirmed from OpenG samples (limitDecendantsTo1Level, Fit VI window to Largest Dec): idx0 array in; idx1 max value; idx2 max index -- feeds Index Array / Delete From Array index ports, confirming it is the index, not the value; idx3 min value; idx4 min index. 1-D scalar-index form only; multidimensional index(es) outputs (which are arrays) are not modeled. Empty array -> index -1 per NI docs, value defaults to 0.

1083.name: First Call?

python_code._body: raise RuntimeError('First Call? (1083) should be dispatched to codegen/nodes/first_call.py by primResID -- this stub should be unreachable')

1083.note: Synchronization palette. 0 inputs, 1 Boolean output. Returns TRUE only the first time the section runs after the VI is run, FALSE thereafter -- stateful per instance, NOT a constant (real boolean constants are bDConstDCO nodes and store their value; this is a class='prim' function with no stored value). Identity confirmed by the NI Synchronization doc + the functional-global 'Changed?' idiom (uninitialized shift register in a run-once loop, OR'd with a comparison). Handled by codegen/nodes/first_call.py (dispatched by primResID, not this template) -- emits a module-level flag seeded True, read then flipped False at each call site.

1057.name: Absolute Value
1057.guess_reason: Was mislabeled 'Array Size'. It is unary scalar X -> scalar X (same type), not an array op, and sits in the numeric cluster (1050-1064), not the array-size range. Confirmed by usage: Subtract -> 1057 -> Increment -> ROI coordinate computes |x1-x0|+1 (a pixel span). This is the integer-typed Absolute Value; 1054 is the same op for extended float (verified by the |a-b|>tolerance compare in failUnlessEqual/passIfEqual), and the two never co-occur. Array inputs would need element-wise handling.

1056.name: Split 1D Array
1056.note: Connector pane: idx=2 is index (numeric), idx=3 is array. Confirmed from pco.camera_FloatingMean_Example.vi instances.

1112.name: Empty String/Path?
1112.guess_reason: Was mislabeled 'Not A Number/Path/Refnum?' (which takes NUMBERS). Observed polymorphic over String (Number to Proper Engl Text) AND Path (Get Class Inheritance from Class Path.vi), both -> Boolean. NI docs (labview-api-ref/functions/empty-string-path): Empty String/Path? 'returns TRUE if string/path is an empty string or an empty path'. The String/Path->Bool polymorphism uniquely pins it.

1145.name: Coerce To Type
1145.note: 1in/1out type conversion. Python is dynamically typed so this is a passthrough.

1510.name: Pick Line
1510.guess_reason: Pick Line primitive (String >> Additional String Functions): chooses the zero-based line_index-th line from multi_line_string and appends it to string; out-of-range index returns the base string unchanged (NI docs). Confirmed a primitive not the vi.lib Pick Line & Append.vi: heap node is class=prim primResID=1510 with no VI-link fields. Observed 5x in Number to Proper Engl Text__ogtk.vi as (I32 index <- Scan From String, String source, String base unwired) -> String -> Concatenate. idx2=multi-line source vs idx3=append-base disambiguated by dataflow: if idx3 were the source it is empty, making the node a no-op passthrough.

1516.name: Select

1999.name: Not A Path

1809.name: Array Size
1809.guess_reason: class=prim primResID 1809 is Array Size (Array[X] -> NumInt32), verified across many samples with varied element types (Path/Refnum/String/Cluster/NumInt32) all yielding a single I32 output. The expandable Index Array is XML class aIndx (resolved by node_type), not this primResID.

1049.name: Sign
1049.guess_reason: Unary, type-preserving numeric op (DBL->DBL, Array[DBL]->Array[DBL]); raw typeDescs confirm both ends NumFloat64. Forced by this VI's direction detection: consecutive angle deltas -> Sign(each) -> Add Array Elements(sum) -> Sign(sum) -> To Byte Integer -> xcreasing in {-1,0,+1}. Only Sign (returns 1/0/-1, type-preserving) collapses the sum to a +/-1 direction; sum (not product) makes it a wrap-robust majority vote. Array inputs would need element-wise handling.

1140.name: To Byte Integer
1140.guess_reason: Conversion to signed 8-bit integer: output is always NumInt8 (or Array[NumInt8]) regardless of input numeric type, verified across corpus (NumInt8/NumInt64/NumInt32/Array[NumFloat64] inputs). NI docs: rounds float to nearest (ties to even) and saturates to [-128, 127]. Scalar template; array inputs would need element-wise handling.

1076.name: Round Toward +Infinity
1076.guess_reason: Unary DBL->DBL. Consumer dataflow pins the mode: String Length (1502) -> /3 (Divide 1053) -> 1076 -> For Loop N count, i.e. ceil(len/3) = number of 3-digit blocks (a 4-digit number needs 2 blocks; only rounding UP is correct). NI docs (labview-api-ref/functions/round-toward-infinity-2): Round Toward +Infinity 'rounds to the next highest integer... equivalent of the ceiling function'.

1167.name: Boolean To (0,1)
1167.note: Polymorphic: Boolean -> I16 (1 or 0). Array of Boolean -> Array of I16. primIndex=69.

1081.name: Logical Shift
1081.note: primIndex=101. Polymorphic on x (any int type). y = shift count: positive=left, negative=right (LabVIEW semantics; Python `<<` only does left).

1053.name: Divide
1053.note: primIndex=106. Polymorphic. Per docs: int/int produces Float64 (matches our 22+ observed instances of NumInt32/NumInt32 -> NumFloat64). Python `/` operator has same semantics.

1111.name: Less Or Equal?
1111.note: primIndex=114. Polymorphic numeric comparison. 7 observed signatures across all integer/float type pairs.

8056.name: File Dialog
8056.note: Interactive UI primitive. Original LabVIEW intent was to ask the user, so we map to Python's input() — runs in CLI, easy to swap with hardcoded Path() or tkinter.filedialog. Configuration Booleans (idx=9, 10) for file/folder/new-or-existing modes are not implemented.

1537.name: To Lower Case

python_code.all_lower_case_string: in_1.lower() if isinstance(in_1, str) else [s.lower() for s in in_1]

1537.guess_reason: Was mislabeled 'Search and Replace String' (an 8-terminal string op); the actual node is a hard 2-terminal (termList elements=2, no unwired terminal), UNARY, type-preserving, polymorphic over String AND Array[String] (auto-maps). Among the four 2-terminal unary string primitives (to-lower-case, to-upper-case, reverse-string, rotate-string), reverse/rotate would scramble word characters and don't fit the number->text role; NI docs (labview-api-ref/functions/to-lower-case): To Lower Case 'converts all alphabetic characters to lowercase... does not affect non-alphabetic characters... polymorphic'. Chosen lower (not upper) because the VI's word output is lowercase (all constants lowercase, conventional English number text). Cleanroom: no glyph available to confirm upper-vs-lower; resolved from VI logic.

python_code.match_rest_of_string: in_4[in_4.find(in_5, in_3):] if in_4.find(in_5, in_3) >= 0 else ''

1170.name: Split Number

1904.name: Multiply Array Elements
1904.guess_reason: Was mislabeled 'Array Size'. Output tracks the element type (Array[UInt32]->UInt32, Array[Int32]->Int32), so it is a numeric reduction, not an I32 count. Sibling of Add Array Elements (1903) in the array-reduction cluster (1910 Or, 1911 And Array Elements). Sum-vs-product settled by context: in 'MultiD Array to 1D Array', 1904(dimension_sizes) feeds a For Loop count -- the total element count of an n-D array is the PRODUCT of its dimension sizes. Empty array -> 1 (math.prod identity), matching LabVIEW.

1903.name: Add Array Elements
1903.guess_reason: Was mislabeled 'Array Size'. Raw typeDesc proves the output is element-typed (Array[NumFloat64] -> NumFloat64), not an I32 count, so it is a numeric reduction, not Array Size (the real Array Size is primResID 1809, Array[X] -> I32). Sits in the array-reduction cluster (1910 Or Array Elements, 1911 And Array Elements). Forced by this VI's logic: sum of per-step Sign(deltas) gives a wrap-robust direction vote. Corpus I32-array instances (sum of int array -> int) are consistent.

1120.name: Sort 1D Array
1120.note: primIndex=206. In OpenG Sort wrappers, sorts ascending; the separately-located 1900 primitive applies Reverse 1D Array to flip to descending. Semantics confirmed: Frame 0 (ascending) passes through 1120 output; Frame 1 (descending) applies 1900 Reverse after 1120 Sort.

1900.name: Reverse 1D Array
1900.note: Polymorphic variant of 1902 (Reverse 1D Array). primIndex=207. Used in OpenG Sort wrappers to flip ascending sort to descending (case frame labeled "descending").
